newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber players sidelined as buyers watch baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber players sidelined as buyers watch baht.

text.p: The Thai rubber market was quiet as most players were sidelined awaiting a clearer picture of the baht after the authorities suddenly floated the currency on Wednesday, trade sources said.
"The rate is very volatile now. Many would rather wait until the baht stabilises and shows clearer direction before making a move," a Hat Yai trader told Reuters.

"But there are a lot of enquiries in the market. Apparently, buyers seemed to see the benefit of coming to the Thai market. But they were reluctant to buy a lot as they would rather wait for what I mentioned earlier," he said.
The central bank on Wednesday changed the currency system from a fixed rate to a managed float, effective immediately.
The move sent the baht tumbling to 28.950/29.450 per dollar in the offshore market from 24.80/25.10 on Monday. Tuesday was a half-year bank holiday for financial institutions.

Although most traders believed the move would benefit Thai rubber exports as it would make the prices cheaper, they said improved competitiveness was likely to be offset by the problem of managing foreign exchange volatility.

"Trading commodities will give you a double headache from now on. In the past, we only handled the price volatility of the rubber itself and did not have to worry about the stable baht," said a Bangkok-based trader.
"Our firm will seek an agreement with banks and clients to sell and buy at certain rates over certain period of time," he added.
The float was expected to pressure regional rubber in the near term as the baht eased against major currencies, making Thai exports attractive.
"The futures prices will drop on selling. Indonesia, for example, is very likely to lower its prices to be able to compete with Thailand," said a trader at a major US trading house.
Benchmark RSS3 for September delivery was offered around 100.00 US cents a kg fob Bangkok. December delivery was quoted as low as 98 U.S. cents a kg on the same basis.
